title: Prebuilt release binaries and download installers
question: How should Lintel ship prebuilt binaries so users don't need Go to install it?
context: Public GitHub repo. Users currently clone and run install.sh / install.ps1, which build with Go. We want the install scripts to download a prebuilt binary for the user's OS/arch and verify a SHA-256 checksum, with no sudo. Module must stay stdlib-only. Jev advice 2026-10-12-how-should-lintel-ship-prebuilt-binaries recommended actions-release.

proposal.choice: actions-release: GitHub Actions workflow on v* tags cross-compiles linux/darwin/windows amd64+arm64 with CGO_ENABLED=0, writes SHA256SUMS, and publishes a GitHub Release with the gh CLI (no third-party actions)
proposal.intent: How should Lintel ship prebuilt binaries so users don't need Go to install it?
proposal.proposed_change: actions-release: GitHub Actions workflow on v* tags cross-compiles linux/darwin/windows amd64+arm64 with CGO_ENABLED=0, writes SHA256SUMS, and publishes a GitHub Release with the gh CLI (no third-party actions)
alternatives: local-release: a local script cross-compiles the binaries and the maintainer uploads them with gh release create by hand
goreleaser: GoReleaser in a GitHub Actions workflow builds and publishes releases
proposal.why: Users install without Go; a tag push builds every target the same way, and the installers verify SHA-256 before installing.
risks: Install scripts depend on the repo URL github.com/Capzay/Lintel and on a release existing.
Binaries stay unsigned, so macOS quarantine and SmartScreen still apply.

invariants.statement: The module imports only the Go standard library.

acceptance_criteria: Pushing a v* tag publishes a release with six binaries and SHA256SUMS; install.sh and install.ps1 download the matching binary, refuse it on checksum mismatch, and install without sudo or admin.
